stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Each of the applicants ___ required to submit a birth certificate.
explanation: "Each" is singular, so it takes the singular verb "is", even when followed by a plural phrase like "of the applicants".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The list of requirements ___ posted on the bulletin board.
explanation: The subject is "list" (singular), not "requirements". A singular subject takes the singular verb "is".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ aware of the new memo.
explanation: With "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Clerks" is plural, so the verb is "were".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The director, along with her two assistants, ___ attending the seminar.
explanation: Phrases like "along with" do not change the number of the subject. "The director" is singular, so the verb is "is".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The documents were given to Maria and ___.
explanation: After the preposition "to", use the object pronoun "me". Test it by dropping "Maria and": "given to me".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Between you and ___, the report is not yet finished.
explanation: "Between" is a preposition, so it takes object pronouns: "between you and me".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
She is the employee ___ received the service award.
explanation: "Who" is the subject of the verb "received". Use "whom" only for objects, and "which" for things, not people.

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
To ___ should the complaint be addressed?
explanation: After the preposition "to", the object form "whom" is required.

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The office will be closed ___ Monday because of the holiday.
explanation: Use "on" with specific days and dates (on Monday, on June 12), "in" with months and years, and "at" with clock times.

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The seminar starts ___ 8:00 a.m.
explanation: Use "at" for specific clock times.

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
By the time the inspector arrived, the workers ___ the site.
explanation: The past perfect "had left" shows an action completed before another past action (the inspector's arrival).

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
If I ___ the head of the agency, I would simplify the process.
explanation: Hypothetical or contrary-to-fact conditions use the subjunctive "were" for all subjects: "If I were...".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The new procedure will ___ the waiting time of clients.
explanation: "Affect" is usually the verb meaning to influence; "effect" is usually the noun meaning a result.

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The agency posted ___ new Citizen's Charter at the entrance.
explanation: "Its" is the possessive form, which is needed here. "It's" means "it is" or "it has", and "its'" is never correct.

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The applicants left ___ folders at the reception desk.
explanation: "Their" is the possessive form. "There" refers to a place, and "they're" means "they are".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
There were ___ complaints this month than last month.
explanation: Use "fewer" with countable nouns (complaints) and "less" with uncountable nouns (less time, less water).

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Of the two proposals, the second one is ___ than the first.
explanation: "Than" calls for the comparative form of "good," which is "better." "More better" is a double comparative.

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The number of online applicants ___ increased this year.
explanation: "The number of..." is singular and takes "has". By contrast, "a number of applicants" means several applicants and takes a plural verb.

stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
explanation: A third-person singular subject takes "doesn't" followed by the base form of the verb: "She doesn't know".

stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: The clerk, who was new, made several errors.
The clerk who was new, made several errors.
The clerk, who was new made several errors.
The clerk who, was new, made several errors.
explanation: A non-essential clause is set off by a pair of commas, one before and one after: "The clerk, who was new, made several errors."

stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: Walking to the office, I saw a long line of applicants.
Walking to the office, a long line of applicants was seen.
Walking to the office, the applicants' line was long.
A long line of applicants, walking to the office, I saw.
explanation: An introductory participle phrase must describe the subject that follows it. Only "I" can be the one walking; the other options are dangling modifiers.

stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: Neither of the two offices is open on Sunday.
Neither of the two offices are open on Sunday.
Neither of the two office is open on Sunday.
Neither of the two offices were open on Sunday.
explanation: "Neither" used as a pronoun is singular and takes "is".

stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quickly and accurately.
The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quick and accurate.
The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quickly and accurate.
The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quick and accurately.
explanation: Adverbs modify verbs. Both "quickly" and "accurately" describe how to complete, and parallel structure needs both in adverb form.

stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: The applicants were asked to bring a pen, a photo, and an ID.
The applicants were asked to bring a pen, a photo, and ID's.
The applicants were asked to bringing a pen, a photo, and an ID.
The applicants was asked to bring a pen, a photo, and an ID.
explanation: Plural subject "applicants" takes "were". "To" is followed by the base verb "bring", and the list items are parallel.

stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error?
[The new employees] [has been] [assigned to] [the records section].
explanation: The plural subject "employees" needs the plural verb "have been", not "has been".

stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error?
[My colleague and me] [were sent] [to the regional office] [last week].
explanation: The subject needs the subject pronoun: "My colleague and I were sent...".

stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error?
[The report must be submitted] [by Friday,] [irregardless of] [the delay in data gathering].
explanation: "Irregardless" is nonstandard. Use "regardless of".

stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error?
[The supervisor] [gave the instructions] [to Ana and I] [this morning].
explanation: After the preposition "to", use the object pronoun: "to Ana and me". Test it by dropping "Ana and": "to me".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The staff were told to ___ their reports before the deadline.
explanation: After "to", use the base form of the verb: "to proofread".

stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The chairman insisted that every member ___ present at the hearing.
explanation: Verbs of demand or insistence take the subjunctive base form: "insisted that every member be present".
